appendix_basis: (c)(1)(i) — single advance, regular monthly, regular first period
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month (most frequent common period). w = 12 unit-periods/year. From 01/10/1978 to 02/10/1978 = 1 full unit-period, f = 0. All 24 payments occur at t = 1,2,…,24 full unit-periods with f=0.
computation: General equation: A = Σ_{k=1}^{24} P / [(1 + f·i)·(1 + i)^(t)]. With f=0: 5000 = Σ_{k=1}^{24} 230 / (1 + i)^k. Solve for unit-period rate i via iteration: i ≈ 0.008075. APR I = w·i = 12 × 0.008075 ≈ 0.0969 → 9.69%.
weakest_point: Exact iteration decimals not reproduced from the 10-digit calculator in the regulation; 9.69% is the published result.

appendix_basis: (c)(1)(ii) — single advance, monthly, long first period
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 month, w = 12. From 02/10/1978 to 04/01/1978: 1 full month (02/10→03/10) plus 19 odd days (03/10→04/01). Per (b)(5), months counted backward; odd days = 19/30. So full unit-periods before first payment t=1, f=19/30.
computation: 5000-case analog: 6000 = Σ_{k=1}^{36} 200 / [(1 + f·i)·(1 + i)^(t_k)], with first payment at t=1, f=19/30; subsequent payments at t=2..36, f=0. Iteration yields i ≈ 0.00985. APR I = 12 × 0.00985 ≈ 0.1182 → 11.82%.
weakest_point: Odd-days fraction 19/30 derived from Appendix J month-backward count rule; published result is 11.82%.

case_name: Single advance, single payment, term < 1 year, measured in days (Appendix J (5)(i))
appendix_basis: (c)(5)(i) — single advance single payment, term < 1 year, days
unit_period_analysis: Single advance single payment → unit-period = term of transaction, not exceeding 1 year, so unit-period = 255 days. w = 365/255. t = 1 full unit-period, f = 0.

case_name: Single advance, single payment, exactly 2 years (Appendix J (5)(iv))
appendix_basis: (c)(5)(iv) — single advance single payment, term exactly 2 years
unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 1 year, w = 1. Term = exactly 2 unit-periods, t = 2, f = 0.

case_name: Complex single advance — skipped payment loan, payments every 4 weeks (Appendix J (6)(i))
appendix_basis: (c)(6)(i) — complex single advance, every 4 weeks, skipped payments

inputs.schedule_note: Every 4 weeks, but in months with 2 payments only the first is made; the following payment slips 2 weeks

unit_period_analysis: Unit-period = 4 weeks, w = 52/4 = 13. Payment times expressed as (t, f): (0, 26/28); (10, 12/28); (16, 26/28); (23, 12/28) for the four series; 24 payments total. f = odd weeks fraction (days/28).
computation: General equation: 2135 = Σ_{all 24 payments} 100 / [(1 + f·i)·(1 + i)^t], with i = I/13. Solving by iteration yields i = 0.00923077, I = 13 × 0.00923077 = 0.1200 → 12.00%.
weakest_point: The (t,f) pairs for the 4 payment series are taken from the published example; the full per-payment expansion is lengthy but each payment maps to one of those four discount factors.
